messages:
Samir (support): FYI customer ACME Health seeing intermittent 429s + high tail latency on their multi-tenant route since they enabled continuous batching this morning. They report spikes around 9–9:30am PST every 10s.

Tara (acme-customer): @Samir here's a quick repro we ran: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rw-large\",\"input\":\"summarize...\",\"stream\":true}'
```
We get a few 200s but ~15% of requests return 429s with request-id header. Example request-id: req_20240317_ak9b2.

Aisha (support): thanks @Tara. Can you paste the request-id and approximate client timestamps for a 429? Also are you using a single API key shared across many clients?

Tara (acme-customer): we use one shared key per product. 429 observed at client ts ~1679050201. We are multi-tenant inside our app so burst from many users at once.

Max (eng-oncall): quick hypothesis: perceived throttling from quota enforcement + continuous batch waiting on KV cache warmup/prefix prefetch. Need router logs + batcher metrics for that request-id. Samir can you pull the router trace for req_20240317_ak9b2?

Samir (support): grabbed logs — pasting sanitized extracts: 
```
[router] req=req_20240317_ak9b2 tenant=acme-health route=/v1/generate queued_ms=78 batch_id=b-113 flush_reason=timeout kv_prefetch=miss
[batcher] batch=b-113 size=1 wait_ms=78 flush=timeout
[quota] tenant=acme-health limit=100rps burst=50 window=60s decision=soft_throttle
[serve] status=429 msg=quota_exceeded
```

Devon (infra): interesting — batch size=1 + wait 78ms suggests continuous batching tried to aggregate but flushed on timeout because KV was not ready. kv_prefetch=miss means prefix/KV cache warmup hadn't populated. If batcher waits for KV keys, small single-request batches can end up with higher latency and fall into quota triggers if many simultaneous tiny batches compete.

Max (eng-oncall): can you also get KV cache hit_rate and prefix warmup queue depth around that time?

Samir (support): pulling metrics, snippet: 
```
kv_cache.hit_rate=0.12
kv_prefetch.queue_depth=42
kv_warmup_latency_p95=210ms
router.batch_wait_p95=95ms
```
These are for tenant=acme-health, time window 9:00–9:30am.

Aisha (support): that hit_rate is very low. Combined with many concurrent small requests under continuous batching, the system ends up spinning up prefetches, causing each request to wait ~100–200ms. When many requests pile up, the quota engine soft-throttles to avoid overload -> 429s. This is "perceived throttling" because the root cause is KV starvation + batching heuristics.

Tara (acme-customer): is there a quick remediation? Our customers are impacted now.

Devon (infra): immediate mitigations: 1) temporary tenant quota bump (increase burst/window) 2) enable aggressive kv-prefetch for the tenant routes 3) suggest client-side smoothing (add jitter / token bucket to spread burst). Max can we do a quick quota patch?

quota-bot: creating ticket Q-4421 to apply a temporary quota bump for tenant=acme-health.

Max (eng-oncall): applied temporary quota bump: new burst=300 for 15m window while we investigate. I also toggled `aggressive_prefetch=true` for acme-health route (no restart). Monitor metrics for next 20 minutes.

Samir (support): pinging @Tara — can you confirm if errors drop after the change?

Tara (acme-customer): after the bump / flag I see 429s drop to ~1% and latency p95 improved ~130ms -> 70ms. Huge improvement, thanks.

Aisha (support): next steps: 1) engineering to tune batcher heuristics so small batches don't block on KV warmup (investigate timeout vs kv-wait tradeoffs) — action: @Max 2) add tenant-level telemetry alert when kv_hit_rate < 0.2 and batch_wait_p95 > 50ms — action: @Devon 3) recommend ACME adopt per-client API keys to smooth bursts and enable client-side smoothing doc — action: @Samir to send doc link.

Max (eng-oncall): will follow up with a follow-up PR to batcher: consider early-flush threshold if kv_prefetch miss > X and batch_size=1 and batch_wait > Y. Also add canary rollout.

Devon (infra): I'll create alert rule PR for kv hit_rate + batch_wait.

Samir (support): noted. @Tara we'll keep the temporary quota bump for 2 hours while we test the change in production. If everything stays green we'll revert and push infra fixes.

Tara (acme-customer): sounds good. Appreciate the fast support. Please keep us posted on permanent fixes.

Aisha (support): closing loop: immediate fix = quota bump + aggressive_prefetch flag. Root cause = continuous batching interacting poorly with cold KV/prefix warmup for tenant causing batch timeouts and cascading quota decisions -> perceived throttling. Followups tracked in Q-4421 and ENG-8772.

Max (eng-oncall): adding ENG-8772 notes: repro steps included above, sample router logs, KV metrics. I'll add a small reproducer script that hits with N concurrent tiny requests to recreate the scenario for local testing.

Samir (support): thanks everyone, marking customer updated. Will post summary to the #incidents channel after we confirm long-term fix. :thumbsup:
